standard.title: Share arts works with audiences
standard.description: share their arts works with audiences
standard.prior_knowledge: No formal prior Drama curriculum. Students have experience of sharing informally in play contexts but have not yet participated in purposeful sharing of arts works with an audience.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students share their arts works — dramatic play, scenes, puppetry — with an audience, and respond to questions about their work.

nodes.label: What sharing means — audience and maker roles
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can distinguish the role of maker/performer from the role of audience, and understand that sharing involves communication.
nodes.minimum_width: Student understands that some people make/perform and others watch, and behaves appropriately as both.
nodes.typical_width: Students participate in informal sharing contexts (gallery walks, performance walks); they use positive language to comment on peers' works, identifying a feature or difference they noticed.
wider: Students explore different kinds of sharing — live performance, digital recording, gallery display — and discuss what changes for the audience in each mode
Students listen to and respond to an explanation from a peer-maker: 'What is going on in your work? Tell me the story.'
nodes.hinge_reason: If students don't yet understand the maker/audience relationship, they cannot engage purposefully with sharing — they perform without awareness of an audience, or cannot attend as an audience member; the sharing event has no communicative dimension.

response_modes.reason: Explicitly name and model the two roles before sharing events; use simple language ('your job as audience is to look and listen, your job as maker is to show your idea').

success_criteria: Student can take on both maker and audience roles appropriately in an informal sharing context
Student can name one thing they noticed or liked in a peer's work

nodes.label: Sharing and talking about the work
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can share an arts work with an audience and describe at least one feature or decision in their work when asked.
nodes.minimum_width: Student shares a piece (however short) with at least one other person watching, and can answer a simple question about it ('What is happening in your work?').
nodes.typical_width: Students present their work to peers; they respond to teacher questions about themes, materials, processes or important features of the work; they use positive language about peers' work.
wider: Students create a simple introduction for their work — describing their favourite moment or explaining why they chose a particular movement or object
Students use a digital device to capture their sharing (with permission) and view the recording, noticing what they communicated
Students retell a story through dramatic play to a class audience using repurposed objects or puppets they have made

response_modes.reason: Sharing integrates all prior making. Teacher scaffolds reflection: 'What did you want your audience to see? What did you enjoy making?'

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The ways Foundation students can share are varied — live, digital, gallery, puppet retelling — and exploring multiple modes of sharing builds early metacognitive awareness of audience and communication.
success_criteria: Student shares an arts work in an informal setting with at least one other person as audience
Student responds to at least one question about their work, describing a feature or decision they made
Student demonstrates attentive audience behaviour when watching a peer's work
